I am a woman of 48 years, farming here in North Central Nigeria. This small plot of beans is close to my house, less than half a hectare, and I intercrop it like my mother taught me — beans help the soil, so I don't waste much money on chemical fertilizer for them. I will put a little of the cattle manure I gather from the neighbors' animals, and I keep my own seed from last year because it grows well here and I cannot afford the hybrid ones from the agro-dealer. My children and I will do most of the work ourselves, but when it is time for weeding and harvest I will call two or three people from the village to help for a few days.
